question: What primary group of people do Maternal and Child Health services specifically target in primary health care?
explanation: MCH services are specifically built around the distinct health needs of mothers and growing children. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why are mothers and young children traditionally grouped together as a single vulnerable population in public health?

options.A: They share the exact same physiological disease symptoms
options.B: Their health outcomes and survival are closely linked to one another
options.C: Government funding requires them to be treated by the same doctor
options.D: Children are solely responsible for providing care to their aging mothers

explanation: A mother's health directly dictates her ability to care for and nurture her child safely. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is one main objective of maternal and child health programs in primary health care?

options.A: Provision of free housing for large families
options.B: Training of traditional bone setters exclusively
options.C: Reduction of maternal and child mortality
options.D: Elimination of all infectious diseases globally

explanation: A core goal of MCH is to lower preventable deaths among mothers and young children. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h2)

question: How do primary health care clinics make MCH services easy for people to access?

options.A: By restricting healthcare access to registered taxpayers
options.B: By requiring patients to travel to tertiary teaching hospitals for routine care
options.C: By bringing essential reproductive and child health care closer to local communities
options.D: By offering services only during late night hours

explanation: Primary health care focuses on community-based delivery to ensure services are within reach of rural families. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h2)

question: What term describes how MCH services flow from before pregnancy all the way through childhood?

options.C: An isolated set of adult clinics

explanation: MCH services link different stages of life together so health care remains uninterrupted. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h3)

question: A woman visits a primary health clinic for family planning advice. What should the midwife recognize about this service?

options.A: It is completely unrelated to maternal and child health outcomes
options.B: It is classified strictly as a pediatric curative intervention
options.C: It forms part of the early foundation of maternal health
options.D: It should only be offered after a woman has completed her family size

explanation: Family planning is an integral entry point into the MCH continuum, safeguarding future maternal and child wellbeing. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which specific care period involves monitoring the mother and baby immediately after delivery?
explanation: Postnatal care focuses on checking both mother and infant during the crucial weeks following childbirth. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of having a skilled attendant present during labor and delivery?

options.A: To manage normal delivery and identify problems early
options.B: To administer routine childhood immunizations before birth
options.C: To diagnose chronic non-communicable diseases in elderly relatives
options.D: To provide long-term family planning counseling for the next pregnancy

explanation: Skilled birth attendants ensure safe delivery and act fast if unexpected complications arise during labor. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which intervention is considered the most effective public health tool for preventing childhood infectious diseases?
explanation: Vaccines prevent debilitating childhood diseases safely and economically at the primary care level. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is growth monitoring an essential part of routine child health services?

options.A: It determines the exact adult height of the child
options.B: It measures the intellectual intelligence quotient of infants
options.C: It serves as a legal record for school admission
options.D: It helps detect early signs of malnutrition and faltering development

explanation: Regular weighing tracks whether a child is growing properly, allowing early intervention if growth slows down. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h5)

question: How do properly spaced pregnancies directly benefit maternal health?

options.A: They allow the mother's body to recover its nutritional and physical strength
options.B: They prevent the occurrence of all genetic disorders
options.C: They eliminate the need for future antenatal clinic visits
options.D: They guarantee the baby will be born during the dry season

explanation: Adequate birth spacing gives maternal organs and nutrient stores time to recover from the demands of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is family planning offered directly inside maternal and child health clinics?

options.A: To reduce the workload of primary school teachers
options.B: To replace the need for routine childhood immunization clinics
options.C: To force community members to limit their family sizes strictly
options.D: To provide accessible contraceptive counseling where women already seek care

explanation: Integrating services makes it convenient for mothers to access family planning while visiting for antenatal or child welfare. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which healthcare professional acts as the main frontline clinical champion for MCH services in primary health centres?
explanation: Midwives manage the day-to-day delivery of maternal and child health services at the primary care level. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h7)

question: A midwife notices that many mothers in her rural area miss their children's second-year immunizations. What is her best duty in this situation?

options.A: Wait until an epidemic breaks out before taking any action
options.B: Punish the mothers by withholding future antenatal care registration
options.C: Refer all children permanently to a tertiary teaching hospital
options.D: Mobilize the community and educate mothers on the importance of complete schedules

explanation: Midwives serve as community mobilizers and educators to bridge gaps in healthcare utilization. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T1#BMP126_U1_T1_h7)
